analysis.investment_thesis: Marc Technocrats is a high-ROIC consulting micro-cap (~36% ROCE) with strong 3-year earnings CAGR of ~41% and a nearly debt-free balance sheet — exactly the business quality the Magic Formula rewards. However, without enterprise value data I cannot compute Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV), making it impossible to confirm whether this quality business is also available at a bargain price.
key_strengths: High Return on Capital: ROCE of 36.27% and implied ROIC ~38% (EBIT ₹10 Cr / Invested Capital ~₹26 Cr) — well above the Magic Formula's 25% threshold
Exceptional earnings growth: Revenue CAGR 35%, Net Profit CAGR 41% over 3 years with expanding EBITDA margins (21% → 23%)
Debt-free, asset-light model: Total debt ₹1 Cr vs equity ₹28 Cr; consulting model needs minimal fixed capital to grow
key_risks: No Earnings Yield data: Without market cap/EV, half the Magic Formula is blind — valuation could easily be excessive for a 41%-growth micro-cap
FCF shortfall vs earnings: Net profit ₹7 Cr but FCF only ₹3 Cr (43% conversion); rapid revenue growth (₹26→₹48 Cr) is consuming working capital
Micro-cap illiquidity risk: Revenue of only ₹48 Cr puts this firmly in SME territory — tiny float, wide bid-ask spreads, and limited institutional scrutiny
red_flags: Exchange listing tagged 'YHD-ERR' — data integrity concern for a listed security
Investing cash outflow (₹4 Cr) exceeds stated capex (₹3 Cr) every year — unclear where the residual ₹1 Cr is being deployed
Promoter holding at 73.55% limits free float further in an already-small company
analysis.detailed_analysis:
On the Magic Formula's return-on-capital axis, Marc Technocrats scores well. EBIT (operating income) of ₹10 Cr on invested capital of roughly ₹26 Cr (equity ₹28 Cr + debt ₹1 Cr − cash ₹3 Cr) implies ~38% ROIC — consistent with the reported ROCE of 36.27%. This is a genuinely capital-light consulting business that is compounding efficiently: every rupee of equity base is earning back over a quarter in operating profit. The 3-year CAGR trajectory (revenue +35%, EBITDA +41%, net profit +41%) shows the high ROIC is not a one-year spike but a sustained trend.

However, the Magic Formula requires BOTH high ROIC and high Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV), and I have zero data on market price or enterprise value. For a ₹48 Cr-revenue Indian SME growing at 40%+ with 36% ROCE, the market almost certainly prices in a fat premium — meaning Earnings Yield is likely compressed well below the 12% threshold that would make this a Magic Formula buy. Additionally, FCF of ₹3 Cr vs net profit of ₹7 Cr (43% conversion) signals that aggressive revenue growth is consuming receivables/working capital, a pattern worth monitoring. Until valuation data is available, this is a high-quality business at an unknown price — interesting, but not actionable under a disciplined formula-based approach.
